proposals.before: The Prince of Yuzhang reported to Emperor Gao. Administrator Wang Ci, Zhang Xu of the Ministry of Rites, and Lu Cheng of the Ministry of the Interior all memorialized on the case. The emperor admired Qianzhi's conduct but feared further blood feuds, and sent him west with Cao Hu.
proposals.after: The Prince of Yuzhang reported to Emperor Wu. Administrator Wang Ci, Zhang Xu of the Ministry of Rites, and Lu Cheng of the Ministry of the Interior all memorialized on the case. The emperor admired Qianzhi's conduct but feared further blood feuds, and sent him west with Cao Hu.
proposals.reason: 世祖 is the temple title of Emperor Wu of Southern Qi (Xiao Ze), not Emperor Gao.

proposals.before: The Prince of Yuzhang reported this to the Founding Emperor; at the time the Administrator of Wu commandery Wang Ci, the Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and the Minister of the Interior Lu Cheng all memorialized on the matter. The Founding Emperor admired his righteousness but feared mutual reprisals, and therefore sent Qianzhi west with Cao Hu.
proposals.after: The Prince of Yuzhang reported this to Emperor Wu; at the time the Administrator of Wu commandery Wang Ci, the Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and the Minister of the Interior Lu Cheng all memorialized on the matter. Emperor Wu admired his righteousness but feared mutual reprisals, and therefore sent Qianzhi west with Cao Hu.
proposals.reason: 世祖 here is Emperor Wu of Southern Qi, not the founding emperor.

proposals.before: He Yin and Xie Tiao were then in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they wrote urging him not to destroy himself in grief.
proposals.after: He Yin and Xie Fei were then in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they wrote urging him not to destroy himself in grief.
proposals.reason: The Chinese name is 謝朏 (Xie Fei), not 謝朓 (Xie Tiao).

proposals.before: At the time He Yin and Xie Tiao were both in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they sent letters earnestly admonishing him against destroying himself.
proposals.after: At the time He Yin and Xie Fei were both in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they sent letters earnestly admonishing him against destroying himself.
proposals.reason: The source names 謝朏, Xie Fei; Xie Tiao is a different person written 謝朓.

proposals.before: Yet honoring gates, renaming lanes, sending grain, and maintaining granaries amounted to little more than pity for widows and orphans and rewards for diligent farmers.
proposals.after: Yet honoring gates, renaming lanes, sending grain, and maintaining granaries amounted to little more than pity for widowers and widows and rewards for diligent farmers.
proposals.reason: 鰥寡 means widowers and widows; idiomatic wrongly renders 寡-pair as widows and orphans.

decisions.reason: s0152’s 言之世祖 / 世祖嘉其義 names Shizu, the temple title of Southern Qi Emperor Wu (Xiao Ze), not Emperor Gao (太祖). Replacing Emperor Gao with Emperor Wu corrects the misidentification and leaves the rest of the idiomatic intact.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 豫章王言之世祖……世祖嘉其義

decisions.reason: The same unit twice refers to 世祖, Emperor Wu, not the founding emperor (太祖). The proposed literal correctly substitutes Emperor Wu for Founding Emperor in both places.
